name: Malignant Triton Tumor
aliases: Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor with Rhabdomyoblastic Differentiation

prevalence.estimate: extremely rare, fewer than 100 cases reported worldwide

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Malignant Triton Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) morphology with areas of rhabdomyoblastic differentiation
Positive immunostaining for S-100 protein and muscle markers such as desmin or myogenin
Rapidly enlarging soft tissue mass often associated with pain or neurological symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of MPNST with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation supported by immunohistochemical staining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other soft tissue sarcomas with rhabdomyoblastic features.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging soft tissue mass with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a firm, deep-seated tumor

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neurological deficits related to peripheral nerve involvement
pathognomonic.notes: Includes numbness, weakness, or paresthesia in affected limb
searchTerms: weakness or numbness from nerve tumor

common.symptomName: Localized pain or tenderness over tumor site
searchTerms: pain or soreness at tumor site
difficulty moving affected arm or leg
tumor site with swelling and heat

occasional.symptomName: Systemic constitutional symptoms such as weight loss
Sensory loss distal to tumor site
Limited range of motion near tumor due to mass effect

searchTerms: fever due to tumor tissue death

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with necrotic areas
CT scan to assess local invasion and metastasis
other: Histopathology revealing spindle cells with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation
Immunohistochemical positivity for S-100 protein and muscle markers (desmin, myogenin)

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of nerve sheath tumor features

redFlags: Rapid tumor growth with neurological deficit
Severe localized pain unresponsive to analgesics
Signs of metastasis such as lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms
references: Gupta G, et al. Malignant Triton Tumor: A Review of the Literature. Sarcoma. 2019;2019:1-9.
Fletcher CDM, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone. IARC; 2020.
